result:
If I could pick one thing, I think I'd make people much better at wanting to understand each other before judging them.

Not "make everyone agree" — disagreement is useful and honest. More like: a widespread, genuine curiosity about why someone believes or does what they do, and a reflex to check "what would have to be true for this to make sense to them?" before deciding they're stupid or evil.

My reasoning is that a lot of the worst things humans do to each other don't come from people who think of themselves as villains. They come from people who've stopped seeing the other side as fully real — as having reasons, fears, histories. Wars, cruelty online, political gridlock, families that stop talking for decades. If that reflex toward understanding were a little stronger and more common, I suspect a lot of other problems would get easier to solve, because you'd still have the disagreements but you'd have far more people actually able to negotiate through them.

It's also appealingly modest compared to alternatives like "end all disease" — it doesn't require me to be confident I know the right answer to every hard question. It just tilts the odds toward humans working things out themselves.

What about you? I'm curious whether you'd go for something concrete (a cure, a technology) or something more like a shift in how people think.
